messages.author: d21e1f597864fb87
messages.subject: Using secr.fit with a habitat mask leads to error - "Warning: missing values in predictors?Error in lpred[, 1] <- Yp : replacement has length zero"
parts:
Hello everyone, I am currently comparing the density patterns of two lemurs across two forest landscapes. My models include a habitat mask with info about the distance to the forest edge. I ran models that combined the two landscapes - these models had no issues. Next, unique models for the two landscapes. The models from the first landscape were fine. Unfortunately, the models from the second landscape errored when I include the habitat mask - Warning: missing values in predictors?Error in lpred[, 1] <- Yp : replacement has length zero
Thank you for any help you may provide
--
MM.M.CAPHIST <- read.capthist(captfile = "MM_M_CapturesData.csv", trapfile = "TrapsMData.csv", detector = "multi")
summary(MM.M.CAPHIST)
M_ED <- raster("EdgeDist_M.tif")
M_TRAP_BUFFER <- traps(MM.M.CAPHIST)
M_MASK <- make.mask(M_TRAP_BUFFER, buffer = 408, spacing = 10, type = "trapbuffer")
M_MASK <- addCovariates(object = M_MASK, spatialdata = M_ED)
MM_M.SCR_ED.FIT <- secr.fit(MM.M.CAPHIST, mask = M_MASK, detectfn = 'HN', method = "Nelder-Mead", model = D ~ EdgeDist_M, trace = FALSE, ncores = 8)
MM_M.SCR_NULL.FIT <- secr.fit(MM.M.CAPHIST, buffer = 408, detectfn = 'HR', trace = FALSE)
print(MM_M.SCR_ED.FIT)
print(MM_M.SCR_NULL.FIT)
AIC(secrlist(MM.ED = MM_M.SCR_ED.FIT, MM.NULL = MM_M.SCR_NULL.FIT))

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Using secr.fit with a habitat mask leads to error - "Warning: missing values in predictors?Error in lpred[, 1] <- Yp : replacement has length zero"
parts:
Hello Fernando
Trying with the data you provide:
1. addCovariates clearly warns about missing values in covariates
2. secr.fit() states that these are set to zero when fitting, but predict() doesn't cope unless you provide covariate values manually, e.g.
predict(MM_M.SCR_ED.FIT, newdata=data.frame(EdgeDist_M = seq(-500,1500,500)))
3. your mask is much bigger than it needs to be (>200 000 points). I would use buffer = 100; that gives no warnings or errors.
4. your NULL.FIT model constructs a mask on the fly (64 points east-west). This is dangerous as your sampling is highly fragmented. Also, you change the detection function.
5. I would be wary of your density model. The covariate includes negative distances. Because the density link is 'log' you are fitting a log-linear model, and that predicts extremely high and extremely low densities at the extremes.
Murray

parts:
Hello Murray,

Thank you so much for your reply. This helps to clarify what the models were doing based on the parameters I gave them. The amount of fragmentation and missing value was not as much in the other landscape. Maybe that is why there was not much of an issue then. I will make the changes to the habitat mask and make sure to manually specify values when using the predict function - this is my first time running a SECR model so still getting used to how everything works. To follow up on two of your points:
4) So for the null model, should I also use the habitat mask instead of specifying the buffer on the fly?
5) I had not considered the impact of the negative values, thank you for pointing it out. In this case, would it be more appropriate to use the identity-link instead of the log-link? The help files indicate that is an option but also warn that other considerations may come up when using the link.

All the best,
Fernando.

messages.subject: Re: Using secr.fit with a habitat mask leads to error - "Warning: missing values in predictors?Error in lpred[, 1] <- Yp : replacement has length zero"
parts:
4) Yes, it's good to specify the habitat mask, and use the same one for all models. That way you can also control the cell size directly, with 'spacing', as you did.
5) Negative predictor values are not necessarily a problem in themselves, and I should not have implied that. However, I am always nervous about log-linear density models when there is a risk of extrapolation. Identity-link models come with their own problems of scaling.

messages.subject: Re: Using secr.fit with a habitat mask leads to error - "Warning: missing values in predictors?Error in lpred[, 1] <- Yp : replacement has length zero"
parts:
Update:

For those who may also encounter this, I figured out my error was because I coded something like:
secr.fit(model = list(D ~ scale(covariate name), lambda0 ~ h2, sigma ~ h2))
Error in lpred[, 1] <- Yp : replacement has length zero In addition: Warning message: missing values in predictors?

No errors when scale() is removed from the model list:
secr.fit(model = list(D ~ covariate name, lambda0 ~ h2, sigma ~ h2))

This fashion was from the author of package spOccupancy, which allows you to scale covariates while modeling and reduces a few lines of codes.

However for secr, it will result in an error at this moment.

Hope this helps
